clue.text: Seafarer discovers vermin food

indicators.note: the second word is pictured revealing the first sitting inside it, as a crust might uncover what is baked within

parts.note: a pie is a food
a rat is a common pest

explanation.surface: A sailor finds a rat in the ship's provisions.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'discovers' as the food uncovering what lies within it, so the pest goes inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A pirate is a robber who sails the seas, so a seafarer by occupation.

clue.text: Used to soften ringing sound at home

definitions.note: a description of the noun: material used to soften

parts.note: a pad is slang for one's home
a ding is the sound of a bell

explanation.surface: Something is used at home to muffle the noise of a ringing bell.
explanation.walkthrough: The ringing sound is placed at the home, which comes first.
explanation.definitionFit: Padding is soft material used to cushion or protect, softening impacts.

clue.text: Tricks confused users

indicators.note: something confused is muddled up and out of its proper order

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Scams baffle people using a computer system.
explanation.definitionFit: Ruses are cunning schemes intended to deceive, so tricks.

clue.text: The man holding the record for place of entertainment

indicators.note: to hold something is to grip it within, so one part encloses the other

parts.note: THE plus Mark, a man's name
an EP is an extended-play record

explanation.surface: Someone holds the world record for an amusement park.
explanation.walkthrough: The man is THE plus MARK; the record EP is inserted after the M.
explanation.definitionFit: A theme park is an amusement park with rides and shows built around a theme.

clue.text: Ignored girl used by 1

definitions.note: points to the answer at 1 across: the thing a pirate uses

parts.note: to cut someone is to ignore them pointedly
a lass is a girl

explanation.surface: A snubbed girl gets used by someone, a sorry social tale.
explanation.walkthrough: The 1 refers to the answer at 1 across, a pirate.
explanation.definitionFit: A cutlass is the short curved sword traditionally carried by pirates.

clue.text: One may be hung and drawn

definitions.text: One may be hung and drawn

parts.note: surface reading: echoes the old punishment of being hanged, drawn and quartered

parts.words: One may be hung and drawn
parts.note: setter's reading: a window drape is hung from a rail and drawn open or shut

explanation.walkthrough: The grisly execution phrase hides a household furnishing.
explanation.definitionFit: Drapes are hung on rails and drawn across windows or stages.

clue.text: Confuse cast

definitions.meaning: second meaning: to hurl or fling

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests muddling a play's actors; the two words are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb means both to disconcert someone and to fling something through the air.

clue.text: Pursuing the invisible man is pointless before evening

indicators.note: a compass point is dropped, leaving the phrase without it

parts.note: to pursue is to go after
nobody can be seen, so no one

explanation.surface: Chasing the Invisible Man is futile before nightfall.
explanation.walkthrough: The invisible man is no one; pointless removes E, a compass point (East).
explanation.definitionFit: The afternoon is the part of the day that comes before evening.

clue.text: Emphasise one's anxiety

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to give weight to

explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as stressing one's own worries.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is a verb for laying emphasis and a noun for strain or worry.

clue.text: Missing a small kitchen item

parts.note: taken as written
S is the abbreviation for small
a tray is a kitchen item

explanation.surface: A little kitchen utensil has gone missing.
explanation.definitionFit: Something gone astray is lost, away from where it should be.

clue.text: Supplier of drugs to woman poet

parts.note: a short woman's name, Diana
Edmund Spenser, author of The Faerie Queene

explanation.surface: A dealer supplying drugs to a female poet.
explanation.definitionFit: A dispenser hands out medicines, as a pharmacist dispenses prescriptions.

clue.text: Run to root out bit that turns

indicators.note: letters that are out of place are disarranged and need sorting

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
R is the cricket abbreviation for a run

explanation.surface: An instruction to dig out a plant's root.
explanation.walkthrough: The run is added to the end of the rearranged word.
explanation.definitionFit: A rotor is the rotating part of a machine, such as a helicopter's blades.

clue.text: Is girl to come out?

parts.note: taken as written
a girl's name

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a young woman is about to make her debut or come out.
explanation.definitionFit: To issue is to emerge or flow forth, as smoke issues from a chimney.

clue.text: Jam-making activity

parts.note: surface reading: boiling fruit and sugar to make preserves
setter's reading: the jam is a traffic jam, caused by repairs to the highway

explanation.walkthrough: The kitchen picture is the trap; the jam is a queue of stationary cars.
explanation.definitionFit: Repairs to the highway narrow lanes and so create traffic jams.

clue.text: Man managed to hide in farm building

indicators.note: one word is concealed inside the other, tucked away within it

parts.note: a man's name
to run a business is to manage it

explanation.surface: A fellow succeeds in hiding in a barn.
explanation.walkthrough: GA(RAN)RY: the managing goes inside the man.
explanation.definitionFit: A granary is a storehouse for threshed grain on a farm.

clue.text: Make a change when a qualification's set in stone

indicators.note: something set in a mount is fixed inside it

parts.note: to alter is to make a change
A plus BA, a degree, with the possessive S

explanation.surface: A rule carved in stone can be changed once someone gets a qualification.
explanation.walkthrough: BA is a Bachelor of Arts degree; the 's supplies the S.
explanation.definitionFit: Alabaster is a fine translucent mineral used for carving, a type of stone.

clue.text: Thought it up during middle of the day

indicators.note: in a down entry, going up means reading from the bottom backwards
something happening during a period sits inside that period

parts.note: noon is midday
taken as written, then turned round

explanation.surface: Someone came up with an idea around lunchtime.
explanation.walkthrough: The turned-round word sits in the middle of midday's four letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A notion is an idea or a belief, a synonym of the noun thought.

clue.text: Who daren't produce more than a one-man show?

definitions.note: a play for two actors exceeds a solo show

indicators.note: to produce is to make, so the letters are made into something new

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Asking which timid impresario won't stage something bigger than a solo show.
explanation.definitionFit: A two-hander is a play written for two actors, so one more than a solo performance.

clue.text: Put away cards on top

parts.note: a pack of cards
to be on top is to be up

explanation.surface: Someone tidies away playing cards placed on top.
explanation.definitionFit: To pack up is to stow things away when finishing, an idiom for putting away.

clue.text: To look mature is a distinction

parts.note: to peer is to look closely
to age is to mature

explanation.surface: Appearing grown-up is something to be proud of.
explanation.definitionFit: A peerage is the rank of a noble, an honour or mark of distinction.

clue.text: French had looked unhappy

parts.note: FR is the abbreviation for French
to have something is to own it

explanation.surface: A Frenchman had a sulky expression.
explanation.definitionFit: To frown is to wrinkle the brow in displeasure, showing unhappiness on the face.

clue.text: Prepare to cook it with tofu

indicators.note: cooking transforms ingredients, so the letters are mixed into a new form

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A recipe instruction for preparing a dish with bean curd.
explanation.definitionFit: To fit out is to equip or make ready, as one prepares a ship for a voyage.

clue.text: Brown has gone off prison

indicators.note: food gone off has spoiled, so these letters are spoilt and reordered

parts.note: dun is a dull greyish-brown
these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A man called Brown has left jail.
explanation.walkthrough: Brown is read as a colour, not a surname.
explanation.definitionFit: A dungeon is an underground cell for holding captives, a kind of prison.

clue.text: Set out to get married when drunk

indicators.note: set out is read as placed out of order and rearranged

parts.note: these letters are rearranged
to wed is to marry

explanation.surface: A couple head off to tie the knot while intoxicated.
explanation.walkthrough: Stewed is informal British slang for drunk.
explanation.definitionFit: Stewed is a colloquial term for intoxicated, one of many slang words for drunk.

clue.text: A sin to play in the river when passing

indicators.note: playing about with something means messing it around into a new order
something in a river is placed inside its waters

parts.note: the Trent is a major river in the English Midlands
these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Swimming in the river as you pass by is considered wicked.
explanation.walkthrough: The Trent is an English river; the rearranged letters go inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Transient means lasting only a short time, just as something passing is fleeting.

clue.text: Plant in under an hour

indicators.note: one item is placed in, so inside, the other

parts.note: sub is Latin for under
HR is the abbreviation for hour

explanation.surface: Planting something in less than sixty minutes.
explanation.definitionFit: A shrub is a woody plant smaller than a tree, such as a bush.

clue.text: Cereal with a type of nut

parts.note: taken as written
corn is a cereal crop

explanation.surface: A breakfast cereal mixed with some kind of nut.
explanation.definitionFit: An acorn is the nut produced by the oak tree.

clue.text: Admit Queen is the one it belongs to

parts.note: to own up is to admit
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the Queen

explanation.surface: A confession that the Queen holds title to something.
explanation.walkthrough: ER, for Elizabeth Regina, is the crossword shorthand for Queen.
explanation.definitionFit: An owner is the person who possesses a thing, so the one it belongs to.

clue.text: Wear out with time in the sea?

definitions.note: the sea is an example of water, hence the question mark

indicators.note: worn out suggests something knocked out of its proper shape

parts.note: taken as written
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: Something is eroded over the years by the ocean.
explanation.definitionFit: The sea is a vast body of salt water, so an example defines the answer.

clue.text: A great many take a cake to a social event

definitions.note: a noun phrase for a large quantity

parts.note: taken as written
a bun is a small cake
a dance is a social gathering

explanation.surface: Lots of guests bring a cake along to a party.
explanation.definitionFit: Abundance means a very plentiful supply, a large quantity of something.

clue.text: Ruled out bringing sailor on board — that''s tough!

indicators.note: ruled out is read as letters put out of order and remade
a passenger taken on board is inside the vessel, so one part goes within the other

parts.note: these letters are rearranged
AB, able seaman, is a sailor

explanation.surface: A sailor is barred from coming aboard, and he is told it's hard luck.
explanation.definitionFit: Something durable is hard-wearing and long-lasting, as tough material is.

clue.text: Continue to forget one''s words at rehearsal?

parts.note: theatre slang: an actor who dries forgets the lines
to run on is to continue

explanation.surface: An actor keeps going after blanking on lines during a rehearsal.
explanation.walkthrough: The pieces are taken in reverse of clue order; the question mark flags the theatrical double meaning.
explanation.definitionFit: A dry run is a practice attempt before the real thing, a trial rehearsal.
